messages:
kai: Heads-up — seeing tail-latency regressions on small decode-only requests since kernel selector changes. Prefill-dominated flows look fine. Suspect mixed-phase batches are forcing wrong kernel picks and thrashing KV cache. Anyone else?

maria: Yup. I measured a p99 bump on Tue aligned with kernel_v2 rollout. Flamegraphs show kernel_select wall time up ~3x on decode paths; kv evictions spike. Mixed-phase batching seems to be the culprit.

chris: That tracks. When prefill+decode end up in the same batch the scheduler uses median seq-len for kernel choice -> bad for short decode continuations. Proposal: maintain phase-tagged queues + separate token_budget targets + kernel affinity.

sam: +1. Also suggest soft cap for decode batch_size so long prefill messages don't overpack the decode kernel. Helps tail latency.

maria: Did a small microbench (A100): mixed batches (4k prefill + 16 decode) show ~40% token throughput drop vs separated batches. Standalone decode batches have stable latency. kv_cache_hits down ~12% during mixed.

kai: Can you share the token_budget config you tried?

maria: Sure — sample config I tested:
```yaml
scheduling:
  queues:
    - name: prefill
      token_budget: 1200
      kernel_pref: kernel_v2
    - name: decode
      token_budget: 200
      kernel_pref: kernel_v1
  separation: phase-tag
```

maria: Also tested kv_prefetch on handoff: enabling `kv_prefetch=true` reduced cold-miss rate by ~8% in the decode queue.

chris: Rollout plan idea: canary 10% with phase-gating + kernel affinity + kv_prefetch. Monitor p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, and kernel_misselect_rate.

sam: Add a fallthrough: if decode queue wait > 15ms, allow cross-phase coalescing but force the kernel to kernel_v1 to avoid misselection penalties.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary/phase-gate-1825 -> nodes: 12

kai: I'll wire up a perf dashboard (p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_misselect_rate) and add an alert for kernel_misselect_rate > 0.5%. Follow-ups: @maria run extended 24h perf run, @chris write rollout playbook, @sam implement soft-cap and fallthrough policy. :thumbsup:
